evidence.computation: For inverse stress/strain requests, the kernel computes the uniaxial linear-elastic relation stress = Young modulus times strain, converts stress units, and refuses nonpositive modulus. It does not establish that a real specimen remains elastic. Other materials requests retain their own named model.
assumptions: Inverse stress/strain requests assume uniaxial linear elasticity and positive Young modulus; supplied inputs and units must describe the intended sample.

evidence.computation: Soil bulk density divides nonnegative dry mass by positive core volume. Soil readers preserve signed exact numeric values and decline malformed numbers.
assumptions: Quantities name the stated dry sample and core; physical inputs satisfy the kernel guards.
untrusted: English quantity roles, units and the shared numeric lexer.

evidence.computation: Dilution preserves stated stock and target roles, balances stock concentration times stock volume against target concentration times final volume, and refuses concentration by dilution. CT arithmetic supports concentration times time and both inverse directions; inverse divisors must be positive and supplied CT/concentration/time nonnegative.
assumptions: Additive solution volumes and a diluent with zero concentration of the solute.
The inherited percent conversion means 1 percent equals 10000 mg/L.
CT uses a constant stated residual concentration in mg/L multiplied by contact time in minutes; the result does not decide potable safety or select a regulatory target CT.
ppm follows the inherited dilute-water convention of mg/L; no solution density is inferred.
untrusted: English quantity roles, units and the shared numeric lexer.

evidence.computation: Uniform scaling preserves quantity dimension and original units: length times s, area times s squared, volume and fixed-density mass times s cubed. Physical base quantities are nonnegative and factors positive. Two successive scales compose by multiplying factors. A typed operation distinguishes absolute multiplication, scale-down division, and relative percent increase/decrease; the effective multiplier is respectively s, 1/s, 1+s or 1-s. Explicit density changes and nonuniform axis scaling are unsupported and refused. Mesh count calculations bind exact nonnegative integer quantities and genus to Euler and closed-triangle incidence equations. Every mesh target validates positive integral implied vertices, edges and faces with nonnegative integral genus; an edge-only query cannot bypass vertex feasibility.
assumptions: Uniform scaling in every geometric dimension.
Mass scaling assumes unchanged material density; volume cannot be inferred from mass alone.
A connected closed orientable triangular surface with stated genus (default zero). Count equations do not establish geometric realizability.
An explicit postfix x or × names an absolute geometric multiplier, including the inherited scaled-up-by-0.5x wording; bare fractional directional factors are withheld as ambiguous.
untrusted: English requested target, original quantity and unit interpretation.
